purpose: Numerical investigation of the reported PlanetIntersection event; this is not a GPU failure reproduction.

reported_event.note: The reported ground_t is a rounded scalar diagnostic. The actual internal FloatPair hi/lo and the PlanetHit status were not included in the supplied event. The scalar must not be treated as the full internal ray parameter.

geometry_parameters.note: The reproduction calls clip and planet_hit directly. These geometry functions do not use the tracking enabled flag, extinction coefficient, scale height, or random samples.

cpu_execution.input_handling: Read through volatile float inputs to avoid compile-time constant folding.
cpu_execution.measured_result: For t_max=infinity and t_max=1e30f, both implementations return clip.status=Ok, hits_ground=true, and planet_hit.status=Ok. The reported GPU failure was not reproduced on CPU.

rounded_reported_parameter_evaluation.note: This evaluates the point at the rounded diagnostic scalar only. It does not establish the residual at the unknown internal GPU FloatPair parameter.

finite_segment_control.note: This finite segment ends before the independently computed sphere intersection. The standalone reproduction intentionally calls planet_hit even though clip.hits_ground is false, violating that function's successful-ground-clip precondition. Its InvalidRay result is a forced negative control, not a reproduction of the user's PlanetIntersection event.

limitations: No actual GPU or OptiX execution of this reported ray was performed in this reproduction.
Ordinary CUDA PTX/SASS inspection is separate evidence and does not prove how the user's OptiX JIT compiled the program.
The candidate preserves explicit FP32 rounding boundaries and improves diagnostics; the available CPU evidence alone does not establish the GPU failure's cause or confirm its resolution.
Long double is used only by the independent CPU numerical reference in reproduce.cpp. Production GPU arithmetic remains FP32.
